column5: An equivalence class of archimedean absolute values of a number field; for a CM field, a pair of complex conjugate embeddings.

column5: A nonzero prime ideal of the ring of integers; its residue cardinality q_w is the order of the residue field. Complex conjugation of a CM field acts on finite places.

The restricted product of the completions E_w over the finite places w with respect to their rings of integers; the subring of integral finite adeles is the product of the O_w. The adele ring is the product of prod_v C (infinite places, via the CM type) with the finite adeles.

column5: For a commutative ring R with involution and a matrix J over R, the group U(J) of invertible matrices g with g^* J g = J, g^* the conjugate transpose.
A sesquilinear form h(x,y)=x^* J y (conjugate-linear in the first variable, as in the Lean source) with J^* = J.
The group GL_n(R) of invertible n x n matrices over a commutative ring R.
The different of a number field E over Q is the inverse of the trace dual {x in E : Tr(x O_E) in Z} of O_E; an ideal of O_E.

The normal subgroup of elements mapped to the identity.
A homomorphism from the additive group of a ring to the multiplicative group of complex numbers (here of modulus one, continuous).

column5: A nonzero left-invariant regular Borel measure on a locally compact group.
An element of a number field that is a root of a monic polynomial with integer coefficients; equivalently integral at every finite place.

For a unipotent group U over a number field E, U(E) is dense in the finite adelic points U(A_f). Used here for the Bessel unipotent group and proved directly from the density of E in A_f (New.besselU_dense).
A group of matrices that are upper unitriangular in a suitable (block) basis.
For a hermitian form h, vectors x, u and a scalar s with h(x,x)=0, h(u,x)=0, s + conj(s) = h(u,u): the isometry v -> v + h(u,v)x - h(x,v)(u + s x).
A vector x with h(x,x)=0 for a hermitian form h; a subspace is totally isotropic if h vanishes on it.
A hermitian plane with basis e, e* such that h(e,e)=h(e*,e*)=0 and h(e,e*)=1.
The determinant of the upper left l x l block of a square matrix (1 for l = 0).

For a square matrix Z over a commutative ring, Z adj(Z) = det(Z) I; in particular the last column c of the adjugate satisfies Zc = (0,...,0,det Z), and its last entry is the leading minor of order one less.
For a linear map f on a finite-dimensional space V, dim ker f + dim im f = dim V; and dim(U+W)+dim(U cap W)=dim U+dim W.

column1: Orthogonal complement for a nondegenerate hermitian form
column5: If h is a nondegenerate hermitian form on a finite-dimensional space V and W a subspace, then dim W + dim W^perp = dim V.
A subgroup of a topological group whose subspace topology is discrete.

column1: Cutoff function for a group action
column5: For a group H with measure nu acting measurably on X, a measurable beta: X -> [0,inf] with integral over H of beta(h x) d nu(h) = 1 for all x; integrals over the quotient H\X of invariant functions are then integrals over X against beta.
The integral of a strongly measurable function with values in a Banach space; in Lean it is 0 when the function is not integrable.
A function beta on a group G such that beta(a^{-1} b) = <u_a, u_b> for vectors u_a of a Hilbert space; then |beta(s)| <= beta(1).
|<u,v>| <= ||u|| ||v|| in an inner product space.

column5: An algebraic integer all of whose conjugates have absolute value 1 is a root of unity. Mentioned in the source only as a remark: integral zeta in a CM field with zeta conj(zeta) = 1 are roots of unity.
The quotient of a local ring by its maximal ideal; for a finite place w of a number field, O_E/w.
The number of cosets of a subgroup; relative index [K : K cap H]. In Lean an infinite index is 0.
The discriminant of the trace form on an integral basis of the ring of integers.
The integral closure of Z in a number field.
A map of groups preserving multiplication.
A homomorphism rho from a group to the invertible linear maps of a complex vector space V; unitary if it preserves an inner product. The group algebra acts by rho(sum x(t) t) = sum x(t) rho(t).

For a linear map A between finite-dimensional inner product spaces, ||A||^2 = tr(A* A) = sum of squared absolute values of the matrix entries in orthonormal bases; it comes from the inner product <A,B> = tr(A* B).
column6: Inner product space; Trace; Adjoint of a linear map

column5: A function on a group that is constant on conjugacy classes.

For a linear map A between finite-dimensional inner product spaces, the map A* with <A x, y> = <x, A* y>.
For a finite family of matrices A_s, the matrix indexed by tuples with entries prod_s A_s(b_s, a_s); the matrix of the tensor product of the linear maps.
